## INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED COAGULASE-NEGATIVE STAPHYLOCOCCUS INFECTION
## (CNS)
Catheter removal is optional. However, treatment is more likely to be successful
with removal of catheter. The decision about whether to remove the catheter
depends on severity of illness, presence of resistant organisms, the need for
the catheter, and how difficult catheter replacement would be.
## _______________________________________________________________________________
## Treatment if the catheter is removed
## Duration of therapy
## Inpatient

In cases where bacteremia is rapidly cleared, treat for 5-7 days. In cases where
rapid clearance of bacteremia does not occur, treat for up to 14 days.
Refer to [coagulase-negative staphylococcus bacteremia](orzid2-gmenu-bacteremia-coag-neg-staph) recommendations for
antimicrobial selection.
Coagulase-negative staphylococcus bacteremia
## _______________________________________________________________________________
## Treatment if the catheter is retained
Consult infectious diseases in all cases. Treatment success rate is improved
when the infected catheter is filled with an antimicrobial solution during
periods when the catheter is not used. Consult Infectious Diseases or Pharmacy
for information.
## Duration of therapy
Treat concurrently with systemic therapy and antibiotic lock therapy for 10 to
14 days. If follow up blood cultures are persistently positive after 72 hours,
catheter should be removed promptly.
## Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.
## Treatment for methicillin-susceptible staphylococci (mecA negative)
Cefazolin 2 gm IVPB q8h ($) [R] <AND> cefazolin antibiotic lock therapy
## Treatment for methicillin-resistant staphylococci (mecA positive)
Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] <AND> vancomycin antibiotic lock therapy
